bugs.title: Demo refresh wipes the Hold Reasons master (5 reasons -> 1 'Token promised')
bugs.evidence: Before refresh (DB + backup test_database-20261116T002006Z taken by the refresh itself): hold_reasons = [Customer interest, Legal/documentation, Management, Pricing review, Token received]. After POST /api/admin/demo-refresh/run finished (done, 00:25:06Z): GET /api/master/hold-reasons -> ['Token promised'] only (browser check refresh-keeps-setup, logged HOLD REASONS ["Token promised"]). After the next backend restart, 4 defaults came back with created_at 2026-11-16T00:32:24 (startup seeding) but 'Token received' is still gone: test_tscheck_refresh_state::test_hold_reason_master_kept -> ['Customer interest','Legal/documentation','Management','Pricing review','Token promised']. Other masters (payment modes, flat types, plans, bank, charge types, projects, tower names, 138 flats, 9 users) and the 3 noted flat prices are unchanged. Hold expiry is mandatory, so a missing reason list affects the Hold flow. Also note: block/project/flat ids are regenerated on every refresh (prices/names identical), which breaks any bookmarked /bookings/new?flat=<id> link.

bugs.title: Right after a demo refresh, System Health 'Last backup' shows 'never' although the pre-refresh backup exists
bugs.evidence: Browser check demo-refresh-today (Settings): 'Demo last refreshed 2026-11-16 · done' OK, but ops-last-backup text = 'LAST BACKUP — never'. Same moment: GET /api/admin/backups -> last_backup: null, archives (6) include 'test_database-20261116T002006Z.archive.gz' = the backup recorded on the refresh's job row. The story rebuild apparently wipes the backups record collection. (It became non-null only later after the JRN-28 manual reseed wrote its own backup at 00:27.) Only the archive count, not the pre-refresh backup name, is visible in the UI.

action_items.detail: My first JRN-26 trigger (00:12Z) was interrupted: I created a test file under /app/backend/e1_tests while it ran, uvicorn WatchFiles reloaded the backend, and the in-process job died, so it never wrote a job_runs row (the reseed itself had finished). I triggered a second clean refresh (00:20:06 -> 00:25:06 done), which is the one the report is based on. Builder hint: DEMO_REFRESH writes its job_runs row only at the end, so a restart mid-run leaves no trace and 'running' silently goes false; consider inserting a 'running' row at start. Data changed by these runs was the sanctioned demo rebuild; my own tscheck rows (tscheck-jrn4 customer, a tscheck plan) were wiped by it and recreated where needed.

Payment plan at 95%: the form shows an inline 'Σ 95.00% ≠ 100' and turns Save off, so you can't save it and no error toast appears. The criterion expects an error toast on save. A valid 100% save shows the success toast 'Plan saved' (sonner). Whether the inline block is acceptable is a spec decision.

Payment form has 5 fields (Booking, Amount, Date, Mode, Bank account) plus an optional Remarks field. With NEFT/RTGS selected it also shows Drawn on bank, Instrument/UTR no. and Instrument date, for 9 visible fields.

The hold register shows 3 active holds but only 1 has an expiry (C-101, about 41.8 h left, 'Token promised tomorrow'). B-101 and B-104 are listed as 'legacy (no expiry)', which conflicts with 'hold expiry is mandatory'.

JRN-28 used exactly ONE manual reseed (00:27Z, POST /api/admin/reseed {confirm:RESEED, story:true}). The reseed recreates users, so the session token is invalidated: the first automated attempt got 401 USER_INACTIVE on the trigger. The trigger was then made right away with a fresh login while the reseed status was 'running'. The test file now re-logs in for future runs and is heavy (it starts a reseed), so run it on purpose only.
